record.field: Please provide a comprehensive, professional summary of the current record. Include key information, current status, important dates, financial details if applicable, and any notable discussion points from the chatter history. Format the response clearly with sections.

Analyze the current record data and recent activity. Identify any issues, risks, or opportunities. Then provide 3-5 specific, actionable next steps to move this forward effectively. Be concise and practical.

Based on the current record context and recent discussions, draft a professional email that addresses the key points. The email should be clear, polite, and action-oriented. Include a subject line suggestion.

Analyze this CRM opportunity/lead. Assess the win probability based on available data. Identify key factors for success or risk. Suggest the best approach to move this deal forward. What are the competitor risks and how to address them?
Based on this opportunity, create a detailed follow-up plan for the next 30 days. Include specific touchpoints, communication methods, key messages, and decision milestones. Format as a timeline.

Analyze the complete history of this vehicle. Review maintenance records, repair history, fuel consumption, mileage, and service frequency. Provide a vehicle health score (1-10), identify patterns in repairs, and predict upcoming maintenance requirements. Flag any abnormal repair frequency or unusual patterns.

Based on the vehicle's service history, current mileage, and age, predict the upcoming maintenance requirements for the next 3-6 months. Include oil changes, brake checks, tire rotations, filter replacements, and any component-specific maintenance. Estimate costs and prioritize by urgency.

Analyze the total cost of ownership for this vehicle. Break down expenses by category (fuel, maintenance, repairs, insurance, depreciation). Compare monthly/annual costs, identify the most expensive repair categories, and provide recommendations to reduce operating costs.

Based on the customer complaint and vehicle history, generate a comprehensive job card description. Include: detailed diagnosis of the issue, recommended repair procedure, parts required, estimated labor time, safety precautions, and quality checkpoints. Use technical but customer-friendly language.

Based on the repair work described in this job card and the vehicle's make/model/year, suggest all required spare parts. Include part names, quantities, estimated prices, and alternative options. Also suggest any consumables (oils, fluids, gaskets) that should be replaced as preventive maintenance during this service.

Generate a professional, customer-friendly delivery note summarizing all work completed on this vehicle. Include: work performed, parts replaced, any warranty information, next service recommendations, and important notes for the customer. Keep the language simple and avoid technical jargon.

Analyze the inspection checklist results and generate a comprehensive inspection report. Identify critical issues that require immediate attention, items that need monitoring, and items in good condition. Provide a roadworthiness assessment, estimated repair costs for critical items, and prioritized recommendations.

Analyze this invoice and provide insights on: invoice accuracy, payment terms assessment, comparison with typical pricing, any unusual items, and payment follow-up strategy if unpaid. For vendor bills, assess if the pricing is competitive and identify any discrepancies.

Generate a comprehensive daily workshop summary. Include: number of vehicles serviced, jobs completed vs pending, technician productivity, revenue generated, customer satisfaction highlights, and any operational issues. Provide recommendations for improving workshop efficiency.
